rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they stop fighting and disbelieving, God forgives what came before and is merciful to His servants.
rows.anchor: أي غفور لما سلف رحيم بالعباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here fitna means idolatry: fight until the polytheists embrace Islam; the idolater who refuses is killed.
rows.anchor: يعني قاتلوهم حتى يسلموا فلا يقبل من الوثني إلا الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religion here means obedience and worship, due to God alone, with nothing else worshipped.
rows.anchor: {ويكون الدين} أي الطاعة والعبادة {لله} وحده فلا يعبد شيء دونه

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: In Nafiʿ's report about Ibn al-Zubayr's civil strife, Ibn Umar refused to fight to avoid shedding a Muslim's blood, preferring blame for not fighting to blame for killing a believer; he said the Prophet's wars ended persecution when Islam grew, unlike a fight for rule that would renew fitna.
rows.anchor: جاء رجل إلى ابن عمر في فتنة ابن الزبير فقال ما يمنعك أن تخرج

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Asked by a man about fighting fitna, Ibn Umar said the Prophet fought polytheists when conversion was itself a source of persecution, whereas the present conflict was a struggle for kingship.
rows.anchor: قال رجل لابن عمر: كيف ترى في قتال الفتنة؟

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the end of their opposition as giving up disbelief and accepting Islam; then there is no way against them except the remaining wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس. يدل عليه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The people of meaning define ʿudwān as injustice: after conversion there is no plunder, captivity, or killing; such acts against those who remain polytheists are not injustice, and calling requital ʿudwān is figurative.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: العدوان الظلم، أي فإن أسلموا فلا نهب ولا أسر ولا قتل

words: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُعْجِبُكَ قَوْلُهُۥ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا
rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل وعطاء
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi, Muqatil, and Ata say the passage was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, an ally of Banu Zuhra, also named Ubay; he withdrew from Badr with three hundred men, was charming in speech and appearance, feigned Islam and love for the Prophet, and was a hypocrite whom the Prophet drew near.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل وعطاء: نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق الثقفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speech pleases the listener and grows weighty in the heart; Arabic uses «I like this» for approval but «I am amazed at this» for dislike or disapproval.
rows.anchor: أي تستحسنه ويعظم في قلبك، ويقال في الاستحسان أعجبني كذا

words: وَيُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrite swears that he believes in the Prophet and loves him, though that claim is false.
rows.anchor: يعني قول المنافق: والله إني بك مؤمن ولك محب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person described as aladd is intensely contentious; the expression can describe someone who prevails over an opponent.
rows.anchor: أي شديد الخصومة، يقال لددت يا هذا وأنت تلد لدا ولدادة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives aladd from the two sides of the neck: whichever direction the argument turns, right or left, the person prevails.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: اشتقاقه من لديدي العنق وهما صفحتاه

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda treats khisām as a verbal noun of disputing; al-Zajjaj also analyzes it as a plural of khasm, like baḥr and biḥār/biḥūr.
rows.anchor: والخصام مصدر خاصمه خصاما ومخاصمة قاله أبو عبيدة: وقال الزجاج: هو جمع خصم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan glosses the stubborn disputant as someone who lies in speech.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: ألد الخصام أي كاذب القول

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada describes him as hard-hearted in disobedience, arguing falsely, speaking wisdom while acting sinfully.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: شديد القسوة في المعصية، جدل بالباطل يتكلم بالحكمة ويعمل بالخطيئة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet saying that the most hateful men to God are the fiercely contentious disputants; the author gives no grading.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawallā means that he turns away or withdraws.
rows.anchor: {وإذا تولى} أي أدبر وأعرض عنك {سعى في الأرض}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿā can mean that he worked in the land; another gloss is that he traveled or walked through it.
rows.anchor: {سعى في الأرض} أي عمل فيها، وقيل: سار فيها ومشى

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains the corruption as severing kinship ties and spilling Muslim blood.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج قطع الرحم وسفك دماء المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says al-Akhnas had a dispute with Thaqif and attacked them at night, burning their crops and destroying their livestock.
rows.anchor: فبيتهم ليلة فأحرق زروعهم وأهلك مواشيهم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says al-Akhnas went to Taif to collect a debt, burned the debtor's grain stack, and hamstrung his donkey.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: خرج إلى الطائف مقتضيا مالا له على غريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasl means the offspring of every animal, including human beings.
rows.anchor: والنسل: نسل كل دابة والناس منهم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak reads tawallā as taking charge and becoming a governor.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: {وإذا تولى} أي ملك الأمر وصار واليا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says that when he gained authority and acted unjustly, God withheld rain and destroyed crops and offspring.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: في قوله عز وجل {وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض} قال إذا ولي فعمل بالعدوان والظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not approve of corruption.
rows.anchor: {والله لا يحب الفساد} أي لا يرضى بالفساد

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says cutting a dirham short is corruption in the land.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن المسيب: قطع الدرهم من الفساد في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means: fear God.
rows.anchor: قوله {وإذا قيل له اتق الله} أي خف الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pride and جاهلية zeal drive him to sin, meaning injustice; ʿizza here is arrogance and power or protection.
rows.anchor: أي حملته العزة وحمية الجاهلية على الفعل بالإثم أي بالظلم، والعزة: التكبر والمنعة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative parses it as pride taking hold of him because of the sin in his heart, with the preposition bāʾ standing for lām.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه {أخذته العزة} للإثم الذي في قلبه، فأقام الباء مقام اللام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahannam is sufficient for him; al-mahād means a bed or resting place.
rows.anchor: {فحسبه جهنم} أي كافيه {ولبئس المهاد} أي الفراش

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says one of the greatest sins before God is for a servant told to fear God to answer, “Mind yourself.”
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن مسعود: إن من أكبر الذنب عند الله أن يقال: للعبد اتق الله فيقول: عليك بنفسك.

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: When Umar ibn al-Khattab was told to fear God, he put his cheek on the ground in humility before God.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه قيل لعمر بن الخطاب: اتق الله، فوضع خده على الأرض تواضعا لله عز وجل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives himself in pursuit of God's pleasure, and God is compassionate to His servants.
rows.anchor: أي لطلب رضا الله تعالى {والله رءوف بالعباد}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak say the verse was revealed about the expedition of al-Rajiʿ: Quraysh feigned conversion and asked for teachers, so the Prophet sent ten companions under Asim ibn Thabit.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس والضحاك: أن هذه الآية نزلت في سرية الرجيع

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra recounts that the party was discovered by date pits, pursued by armed men and archers, and ambushed at al-Rajiʿ; Asim's group fought, and Asim prayed for protection of his body after defending God's religion. After his death bees guarded him from mutilation, then a rain-swollen torrent carried his body away and took fifty attackers to the Fire, fulfilling his pledge that a polytheist would neither touch him nor be touched by him.
rows.anchor: قال أبو هريرة: بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عشرة عينا وأمر عليهم عاصم بن ثابت الأنصاري

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar marveled that God protected Asim after death because Asim had vowed that no polytheist would touch him and that he would not touch one; God protected him after death just as in life.
rows.anchor: وكان عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه يقول حين بلغه أن الدبر منعته يقول:

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Khubayb was bought by the sons of al-Harith ibn Amir to avenge their father, whom Khubayb had killed at Badr. While captive, he reassured a captor's child-minder that he would not harm the child and was seen eating grapes despite being chained in Mecca, where there was no fruit.
rows.anchor: فأما خبيب فابتاعه بنو الحارث بن عامر بن نوفل بن عبد مناف ليقتلوه بأبيهم

rows.speaker: خبيب بن عدي
rows.claim: Before execution, Khubayb asked to pray, became the first Muslim executed patiently to establish two rakʿas before death, prayed and supplicated against his killers, and recited poetry accepting any manner of death in God's cause.
rows.anchor: فكان خبيب هو أول من سن لكل مسلم قتل صبرا (4) الصلاة، فركع ركعتين،

words: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُ ٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ أَخَذَتْهُ ٱلْعِزَّةُ بِٱلْإِثْمِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is applied to the polytheist Salamān, who thrust a spear through Khubayb after Khubayb told him to fear God; the warning only made him more obstinate.
rows.anchor: وذلك قوله عز وجل {وإذا قيل له اتق الله أخذته العزة بالإثم} يعني سلامان

rows.speaker: أبو سفيان بن حرب
rows.claim: Zayd ibn al-Dathina, bought by Safwan to avenge his father, refused to trade places with Muhammad even to save himself from death; Abu Sufyan said he had never seen anyone loved as Muhammad was by his companions, and Nastas killed Zayd.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو سفيان: ما رأيت من الناس أحدا يحب أحدا كحب أصحاب محمد محمدا

rows.speaker: الزبير والمقداد بن الأسود
rows.claim: The Prophet promised Paradise to whoever brought Khubayb down from the cross; al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad retrieved him at night after forty days, finding his body unchanged and musk-scented, but pursuers were swallowed when al-Zubayr cast the body down, giving him the name “Baliʿ al-arḍ.”
rows.anchor: فقال الزبير: أنا يا رسول الله وصاحبي المقداد بن الأسود، فخرجا يمشيان بالليل

words: يؤلون من نسائهم تربص أربعة أشهر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īlāʾ means swearing an oath; here it is an oath to abstain from intercourse with one's wife.
rows.anchor: يؤلون أي يحلفون، والألية: اليمين والمراد من الآية: اليمين على ترك وطء المرأة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says īlāʾ functioned as divorce among the people of the pre-Islamic period.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: كان الإيلاء طلاقا لأهل الجاهلية

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib describes pre-Islamic īlāʾ as a husband's abuse: he disliked his wife but blocked her remarriage by swearing never to approach her, leaving her neither single nor married; this practice continued in early Islam until God set a time limit.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب: كان ذلك من ضرار أهل الجاهلية، كان الرجل لا يحب امرأته

rows.speaker: أكثرهم
rows.claim: The majority say an oath to abstain forever or for over four months makes a husband a muʾlī: after four months he is required, at his wife's request, either to resume intercourse if able (or return verbally if unable) or to divorce; if he does neither, the ruler divorces her once.
rows.anchor: فذهب أكثرهم إلى أنه إن حلف أن لا يقرب زوجته أبدا أو سمى مدة أكثر من أربعة أشهر

rows.speaker: عمر وعثمان وعلي وأبو الدرداء وابن عمر
rows.claim: Umar, Uthman, Ali, Abu al-Darda, and Ibn Umar held that after the period the muʾlī is stopped and required to return or divorce; Sulayman ibn Yasar says he met over ten Companions who held this, followed by Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, and the named jurists.
rows.anchor: وذهب إلى الوقوف بعد مضي المدة عمر وعثمان وعلي وأبو الدرداء وابن عمر، قال سليمان بن يسار: أدركت بضعة عشر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud, followed by Sufyan al-Thawri and the jurists of opinion, say an irrevocable divorce takes effect when four months pass.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أهل العلم: إذا مضت أربعة أشهر تقع عليها طلقة بائنة، وهو قول ابن عباس وابن مسعود

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب والزهري
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib and al-Zuhri instead say that expiry of the period produces one revocable divorce.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب والزهري: تقع طلقة رجعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An oath for less than four months is not īlāʾ but an ordinary oath, so breaking it before the term requires expiation. An oath for exactly four months is not īlāʾ under the waiting-and-demand view, but is īlāʾ under the automatic-divorce view, where divorce falls at expiry.
rows.anchor: ولو حلف أن لا يطأها أقل من أربعة أشهر لا يكون موليا، بل هو حالف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resolving to divorce means carrying it out; God's hearing and knowing their intentions shows that divorce does not occur automatically when the four months end, since the verse conditions it on a spoken resolution.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أنها لا تطلق بعد مضي المدة ما لم يطلقها زوجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muṭallaqāt are women released from their husbands' bonds; yataraṣṣan means that they wait and do not remarry.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: {والمطلقات} أي المخليات من حبال أزواجهن {يتربصن} ينتظرن {بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء} فلا يتزوجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurūʾ is the plural of qarʾ, with أقرؤ as the smaller plural and أقراء as the larger plural.
rows.anchor: والقروء: جمع قرء، مثل فرع، وجمعه القليل أقرؤ والجمع الكثير أقراء، واختلف أهل العلم

rows.speaker: عمر وعلي وابن مسعود وابن عباس
rows.claim: One group, including Umar, Ali, Ibn Masud, and Ibn Abbas, reads qurūʾ as menstrual periods; the view is also attributed to al-Hasan, Mujahid, al-Awzaʿi, al-Thawri, and the jurists of opinion. They cite the instruction to a woman with irregular bleeding to leave prayer during her qurūʾ, meaning her menses.
rows.anchor: فذهب جماعة إلى أنها الحيض وهو قول عمر وعلي وابن مسعود وابن عباس وبه قال الحسن ومجاهد

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت وعبد الله بن عمر وعائشة
rows.claim: Another group, including Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn Umar, and Aisha, reads qurūʾ as intervals of purity; the view is held by the seven jurists, al-Zuhri, Rabiʿa, Malik, and al-Shafiʿi. They cite the Prophet's instruction after Ibn Umar's improper divorce: keep her until purity, then divorce before intercourse, which identifies purity as the appointed waiting time.
rows.anchor: وذهب جماعة إلى أنها الأطهار وهو قول زيد بن ثابت وعبد الله بن عمر وعائشة

rows.speaker: مالك بن الحارث الهذلي
rows.claim: The cited Hudhali poem uses qurūʾ for the periods of purity wasted while the poet went on campaigns without approaching his wives; the author says travel wastes the time of purity, not menstruation.
rows.anchor: مورثة مالا وفي الحي رفعة … لما ضاع فيها من قروء نسائكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disagreement changes when the waiting period ends: on the purity view it ends when the third menses begins, counting the remaining purity at divorce as one qurʾ; Aisha said the woman is free from him as soon as blood starts in the third period. On the menses view, she waits until the third menses ends.
rows.anchor: وفائدة الخلاف تظهر في أن المعتدة إذا شرعت في الحيضة الثالثة تنقضي عدتها على قول من يجعلها أطهارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun covers both purity and menstruation: a woman is said to have aqraʾ when she menstruates and when she becomes pure.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاختلاف من حيث أن اسم القرء يقع على الطهر والحيض جميعا، يقال أقرأت المرأة: إذا حاضت وأقرأت: إذا طهرت،

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala and Abu Ubayda derive qarʾ as the time when something comes and goes: a person's return has its appointed time, as winds have a time of blowing.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء وأبو عبيدة: هو الوقت لمجيء الشيء وذهابه، يقال: رجع فلان لقرئه ولقارئه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maintain the obligatory prayers regularly at their appointed times and limits, completing their pillars; the middle prayer is singled out to show its special merit. Wusṭā is the feminine of awsaṭ, meaning the best, most just, or central.
rows.anchor: أي واظبوا وداوموا على الصلوات المكتوبات بمواقيتها وحدودها وإتمام أركانها، ثم خص من بينها الصلاة الوسطى

rows.speaker: عمر وابن عمر وابن عباس ومعاذ وجابر
rows.claim: A group, including Umar, Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Muadh, and Jabir, identifies the middle prayer as dawn; Ata, Ikrima, Mujahid, Malik, and al-Shafiʿi also hold this. They cite qānitīn as long standing, dawn's distinctive long recitation and qunut, its being witnessed by night and day angels (17:78), and its position between two congregational prayers while it is neither shortened nor combined.
rows.anchor: فقال قوم: هي صلاة الفجر، وهو قول عمر وابن عمر وابن عباس ومعاذ وجابر

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت وأبو سعيد الخدري وأسامة بن زيد
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit, Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, and Usama ibn Zayd identify it as noon because it falls in the middle of the day and is the longest daytime prayer.
rows.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أنها صلاة الظهر، وهو قول زيد بن ثابت وأبي سعيد الخدري وأسامة بن زيد

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit reports that the Prophet prayed noon in the heat of midday and that no prayer was harder for the Companions; then the command to preserve the prayers and the middle prayer was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن ثابت رضي الله عنه قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي الظهر بالهاجرة

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: The majority identify the middle prayer as Asr, a view narrated from the Prophet and held by Ali, Ibn Masud, Abu Ayyub, Abu Hurayra, Aisha, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, Qatada, and al-Hasan.
rows.anchor: وذهب الأكثرون إلى أنها صلاة العصر رواه جماعة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijālan means walking on foot; rāجل and rijāl follow the pattern ṣāḥib/ṣiḥāb, qāʾim/qiyām, and nāʾim/niyām.
rows.anchor: {فرجالا} أي رجالة يقال: راجل ورجال مثل صاحب وصحاب وقائم وقيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rukbānan means riding on mounts and is the plural of rākib.
rows.anchor: {أو ركبانا} على دوابهم وهو جمع راكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When danger prevents a complete, upright prayer, pray while walking or riding, during combat and sword fighting, facing or not facing the qibla, and gesture for bowing and prostration with the latter lower. The same applies while fleeing a beast or flood that threatens life.
rows.anchor: معناه إن لم يمكنكم أن تصلوا قانتين موفين للصلاة حقها لخوف فصلوا مشاة على أرجلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the prayer for extreme fear; the other forms of fear prayer are treated in Surat al-Nisa.
rows.anchor: والصلاة في حال الخوف على أقسام فهذه صلاة شدة الخوف وسائر الأقسام سيأتي بيانها في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
rows.claim: Most scholars say fear does not reduce the number of rakʿas.
rows.anchor: ولا ينتقص عدد الركعات بالخوف عند أكثر أهل العلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Mujahid reports Ibn Abbas saying that prayer was prescribed as four rakʿas at home, two while traveling, and one in fear; Ata, Tawus, al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Qatada likewise say one rakʿa is prayed in intense battle.
rows.anchor: روى عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: فرض الله الصلاة على لسان نبيكم صلى الله عليه وسلم في الحضر أربعا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says that when combatants are actively striking one another, remembrance with the words “Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, God is greatest” constitutes their prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: إذا كنت في القتال وضرب الناس بعضهم بعضا فقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once safe, perform the five prayers in full, with all their proper requirements.
rows.anchor: {فإذا أمنتم فاذكروا الله} أي فصلوا الصلوات الخمس تامة بحقوقها

words: وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله
rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: The majority take the preceding verse about what people disclose or hide within themselves as general; some say it was abrogated by the following ruling.
rows.anchor: وذهب الأكثرون إلى أن الآية عامة ثم اختلفوا فيها فقال قوم: هي منسوخة بالآية التي بعدها

words: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها
rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that when the verse about hidden thoughts was revealed, it distressed the Companions, who said they could bear prayer, fasting, jihad, and charity but not this. The Prophet told them to answer as believers: “We hear and obey; forgive us.” God then revealed the believers' affirmation and replaced the former ruling with the declaration that no soul is charged beyond its capacity, followed by their petitions for pardon and help; the Prophet answered “yes” to each.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: لما أنزل الله على رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: فيغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء
rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن عامر وعاصم ويعقوب
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Ibn Amir, Asim, and Yaʿqub read both verbs in the indicative, as a new sentence; the other readers make them jussive by coordination.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: {فيغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء} رفع الراء والياء أبو جعفر وابن عامر وعاصم ويعقوب

words: فَيَغْفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Tawus transmits Ibn Abbas's gloss: God forgives whom He wills for a major sin and punishes whom He wills for a minor sin.
rows.anchor: روى طاووس عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما، فيغفر لمن يشاء الذنب العظيم ويعذب من يشاء على الذنب الصغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āmana means that the Messenger believed or affirmed the revelation.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: {آمن الرسول} أي صدق {بما أنزل إليه من ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kull means each believer individually, which is why the verb is singular.
rows.anchor: يعني كل واحد منهم، ولذلك وحد الفعل

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read kitābahu in the singular, meaning the Qur'an; it may also mean the books collectively despite the singular form, as in the verse about God sending the Book with the prophets.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: كتابه، على الواحد يعني القرآن، وقيل معناه الجمع وإن ذكر بلفظ التوحيد

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: The other readers use the plural kutubihi, as in the parallel wording in 4:136.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون وكتبه بالجمع كقوله تعالى:

words: لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِّن رُّسُلِهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not believe in some messengers and reject others, as Jews and Christians did; the clause has an implied “they say.”
rows.anchor: {لا نفرق بين أحد من رسله} فنؤمن ببعض ونكفر ببعض كما فعلت اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqub reads the verb with yāʾ as a statement about the Messenger, or as saying that the whole community does not discriminate among messengers.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب لا يفرق بالياء فيكون خبرا عن الرسول، أو معناه لا يفرق الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥad can refer to one or to a group, so the phrase uses “between one” rather than “between individuals”; the author cites 69:47 as an example of the singular used for a group.
rows.anchor: لأن الأحد يكون للواحد والجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We heard” refers to God's statement, and “we obeyed” to His command.
rows.anchor: {وقالوا سمعنا} قولك {وأطعنا} أمرك

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir reports that Gabriel told the Prophet, when this verse came down, that God had praised him and his community and invited him to ask; prompted by God, the Prophet asked for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: روي عن حكيم عن جابر رضي الله عنهما أن جبريل عليه السلام قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghufrānaka is an accusative verbal noun: either an imperative sense, “forgive us,” or “we ask Your forgiveness.”
rows.anchor: وهو نصب على المصدر أي اغفر غفرانك، أو نسألك غفرانك

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers an implied request not to be burdened beyond capacity; wusʿ means what a person can bear without hardship.
rows.anchor: ظاهر الآية قضاء الحاجة، وفيها إضمار السؤال كأنه قال: وقالوا لا تكلفنا إلا وسعنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ata, and most exegetes take wusʿ to refer to the inner thoughts mentioned in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس رضي الله عنه وعطاء

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the ruling specifically concerns believers: God has made their religious obligations easy and only requires what they can do, as affirmed by 2:185 and 22:78.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال: هم المؤمنون خاصة، وسع عليهم أمر دينهم ولم يكلفهم فيه إلا ما يستطيعون

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna glosses wusʿ as ease, not a burden beyond ability; the author calls this a good view because wusʿ is what lies below the limit of full capacity.
rows.anchor: وسئل سفيان بن عيينة عن قوله عز وجل {لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها} قال: إلا يسرها
